messages.author: b4aaa9a07a2ce407
messages.subject: What is the equivalent of ggplot2:ScaleLog10 in the new version of ggplot.
parts:
In the release version of ggplot2 I hacked up my own log scale with breaks that suited my purposes.
How would I go about this with the new scales package (no ScaleLog10 in the new ggplot).


ScaleLogtime <- proto(ScaleLog10, funEnvir = globalenv(), {
    objname = "logtime"
    desc = "Position scale, time in seconds log10 transformed"
    doc=FALSE
    examples=function(.) {}

    ## Calculate our own breaks and labels and hand them off to ScaleLog10.
    ## It might be better to override the ScaleContinuous functions because
    ## when then data range is known, so could chose breaks based on that.
    new <- function(., ...)
    {
        ##print(c("ScaleLogtime$new",.,...))
        minors <- c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9)
        majors <- c(1,2,5)
        breaks <- c(c(1,5)*0.01, majors*0.1, majors*1, c(10,30),
                    majors*60, c(10,20)*60, majors*3600, majors*3600*10)
        minor_breaks <- c(minors*0.01, minors*0.1, minors, c(1,2,3,4,5)*10,
                          minors*60, minors*600, minors*3600, minors*3600*10)
        labels <- lapply(breaks,function(t) {
            if (t < 0.1)
                paste(formatC(t*1000,format="fg"),"ms",sep="")
            else if (t < 60)
                paste(formatC(t,format="fg"),"s",sep="")
            else if (t < 3600)
                paste(formatC(t/60,format="fg"),"m",sep="")
            else
                paste(formatC(t/3600,format="fg"),"h",sep="")
        })
        .super$new(.,breaks=breaks,labels=labels,minor_breaks=minor_breaks,...)
    }
})

messages.author: b4aaa9a07a2ce407
messages.subject: Re: What is the equivalent of ggplot2:ScaleLog10 in the new version of ggplot.
parts:
I have typically been using this for cumulative density functions of 
game server session lifetimes (http://www.monkeyquest.com).  
The session lifetimes can range from seconds to hours, hence the log time scale.

    ggplot(d)
     + geom_line(size=1,aes(x=lifetime,y=percent,color=qos))
     + scale_x_logtime(name=xlab) 

Looking at the new code I guess I do this...

    scale_x_logtime <- function(...) {
        scale_x_continuous(..., trans = log10_trans(), breaks = logtime.breaks, labels = logtime.labels)
    }

where logtime.breaks and labels are functions that take limits as an arg.

But what is the right way to handle the minor breaks?  
Its important that the time units be "friendly" seconds, minutes and hours 
so for example they go 10,20,30,40,50 secs, then jump to 1min, 2min, 3min, etc.  
I see there is an internal function scale_breaks_minor but I doubt it will produce what I want. 
How do I override that just for my scale? 
Do I need to create a new S3 coord and handle that in coord_train?
